title: Bistability of Exciton-Photon Microcavities in the Ultrastrong-Coupling Regime
authors: Rashed Aljasmi, Hisham Sati, Hichem Eleuch
abstract: We investigate a coherently driven exciton--photon microcavity with Kerr nonlinearity in the ultrastrong-coupling regime. When the lower and upper polariton branches are well separated in energy, the full Hopfield--Rabi--Kerr model reduces to an effective single-mode description of the lower polariton. We analyze the stability of the lower-polariton steady states. We show that the resulting bistability is qualitatively similar to that in the strong-coupling regime. However, in the ultrastrong-coupling regime counter-rotating processes and the diamagnetic $A^{2}$ term renormalize the polariton spectrum and composition, changing the effective detuning $\tildeΔ_{1}$ and nonlinearity $U_{\mathrm{LP}}$ $g$-dependency beyond the strong-coupling (RWA) picture. As a result, although the semiclassical bistability criterion keeps its standard Kerr--oscillator form, the turning points and hysteresis window are shifted relative to the strong-coupling prediction.
summary: The paper theoretically analyzes bistability in semiconductor microcavities operating under ultrastrong coupling. By retaining counter-rotating terms beyond the standard RWA, the authors show that while the qualitative physics remains similar to strong coupling, quantitative predictions for hysteresis loops are significantly shifted due to spectral renormalization.
main_problem: The study investigates the phenomenon of optical bistability in exciton-photon microcavities when operating within the ultrastrong-coupling regime.
main_result: While the bistability retains a standard Kerr-oscillator form, the inclusion of counter-rotating processes and diamagnetic terms renormalizes the polariton spectrum, causing measurable shifts in the turning points and hysteresis window compared to predictions from the strong-coupling (RWA) limit.
method: The analysis uses a mean-field approximation on the effective single-mode Hamiltonian derived after diagonalizing the full Hopfield-Rabi model using Bogoliubov transformations.
model_or_system: The system is an exciton-photon microcavity modeled by a Hamiltonian including Rabi coupling, Kerr nonlinearity, and external driving. The dynamics are treated via a Lindblad master equation for the lower polariton branch approximation.
key_observables: Bistability (S-shaped input-output curves), polariton frequencies ($\omega_{1,2}$), effective detuning ($	ilde{\Delta}_1$), and nonlinearity ($U_{\mathrm{LP}}$).
important_parameters: Ultrastrong-coupling regime ($\eta \gtrsim 0.1$), coupling strength ($g$), and the diamagnetic term $D$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a weakly nonlinear regime, allowing for an effective single-mode description (lower polariton approximation), and explicitly neglects phase-space filling effects.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how the lower and upper polariton frequencies depend on the coupling strength $g$ and other parameters.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the full Hamiltonian formulation, reduces it to an effective single-mode description via polariton diagonalization, derives the semiclassical equations of motion using a mean-field approach, and finally analyzes stability criteria to map out the bistability regions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes beyond the standard Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA) in cavity QED systems, showing how fundamental quantum corrections (counter-rotating terms) alter macroscopic nonlinear phenomena like optical switching.

In both panels, solid lines correspond to the full model including the diamagnetic term D, while dashed lines correspond to the case where the diamagnetic term is neglected (D = 0). Blue and orange curves denote the UP and LP branches, respectively. Including D produces an overall blueshift of both polariton branches, which becomes more pronounced at larger coupling.
